accessibility_contract: Screen-reader-first: every state change announced via ARIA live regions, focus never lost, no color-only information, large touch targets, plain-language everything. See ACCESSIBILITY.md.
contact: Built by Mary Robinson — this manifest is the pitch: the integration points are live and waiting; Meta just has to plug in.

custom_protocol.note: Registered via manifest.json protocol_handlers (installed PWA, Chromium browsers). The app unwraps the scheme and runs the action.

actions.true-access/describe: Runs the describe flow. Returns { ok:true } or { ok:false, error:'not-listening' } when mic consent is still needed
actions.true-access/ping: Returns { ok:true, app:'true-access', version } — capability probe
actions.true-access/repeat: Repeats the last description. Returns { ok:true }
actions.true-access/stop: Stops listening and speech. Returns { ok:true }

honest_limits: Browsers only grant microphone access after a user gesture; a remote describe while listening is off queues the flow and reports not-listening rather than failing silently
iOS suspends web audio when the screen locks or Safari backgrounds — a native host fixes this
postmessage_api.target: Embed True Access in a webview/iframe and drive it with window.postMessage

actions.describe: ?action=describe — start listening (if needed) and describe what's playing
actions.repeat: ?action=repeat — speak the last description again (no microphone needed)

url_actions.autostart: Append &autostart=1 to begin immediately on page load

no_credits_pledge: Every third-party service in True Access is free with no credit system, no pay-as-you-go, and no expiring trial. If a service needs credits, it is not used.

on_device_tech.ai_description: Keyless free LLM providers (Pollinations, LLM7) — no accounts, no credits; optional free Gemini key for better quality
on_device_tech.fingerprinting: Chromaprint (WebAssembly, MIT-licensed, vendored) — audio never leaves the phone except the fingerprint string
on_device_tech.wake_word: Porcupine on-device wake word (free tier, no credits, no card) with browser speech recognition fallback

tagline: Real-time audio description for everything you watch — TV, phone, tablet, or computer.
what_it_does: Captures nearby audio through the phone microphone (including the Ray-Ban Meta glasses paired as a Bluetooth headset)
Identifies music via on-device audio fingerprinting (Chromaprint WASM + free AcoustID lookup)
Checks a curated database of official audio-description tracks and tells the user where to enable them
Generates an AI visual overview via free, keyless LLM providers when no official track exists
Speaks the description aloud through the phone or glasses speakers
Hands-free voice trigger: say "describe this" or "audio describe" — on-device wake word (Porcupine) or browser speech recognition

what_meta_needs_to_provide.title: Route 'Hey Meta, describe this' to True Access
what_meta_needs_to_provide.why: Today the glasses' own assistant swallows any phrase starting with 'Hey Meta' before this app ever hears it. Only Meta can route the phrase to True Access natively on the glasses.

what_meta_needs_to_provide.title: Supported microphone + speaker path between glasses and phone app
what_meta_needs_to_provide.why: Today the app depends on the glasses pairing as a generic Bluetooth headset and the OS handing the browser some microphone. A supported path makes the trigger reliable.

what_meta_needs_to_provide.title: Background audio for descriptions
what_meta_needs_to_provide.why: iOS suspends web audio when the screen locks or Safari backgrounds. A native path (or glasses-side processing) keeps descriptions playing with the phone in a pocket.

what_meta_needs_to_provide.title: Content identification backend (the Shazam piece)
what_meta_needs_to_provide.why: No free service fingerprints TV/movie audio — only music databases are free and open. Enterprise identification (Gracenote/ACRCloud class) is the funded milestone.

what_meta_needs_to_provide.title: Official audio-description track access
what_meta_needs_to_provide.why: Streaming AD tracks are DRM-locked inside their apps. Today True Access can only tell the user where the track is and how to enable it — with Meta's help it could hand off or play the real track.

what_meta_needs_to_provide.title: Camera access on the glasses (future)
what_meta_needs_to_provide.why: Third-party apps cannot touch the glasses' camera today. True visual context — real moment-by-moment description — needs Meta to open it or build it natively.
